passages.provision_quote: On and after January 1, 2025, an agency responsible for the development or operation of bikeways or highways where bicycle travel is permitted shall not install a new sharrow on a highway that has a posted speed limit greater than 30 miles per hour, except at or near an intersection for the purpose of connecting a Class I, Class II, or Class IV bikeway through the intersection.
passages.note: A design standard that bars sharrows and Class III bikeways from fast roads and from the Active Transportation Program's eligible projects; it sets no share of investment between modes.

rows.reasoning: The only source is SB 1216 (2023-2024), which Blakespear authored; its operative sections prohibit installing "a new sharrow on a highway that has a posted speed limit greater than 30 miles per hour" and bar the commission from adding Class III bikeway projects to the Active Transportation Program's program of projects. That governs the design quality of bicycle facilities inside an existing active-transportation program; it does not say whether to "Prioritize pedestrian infrastructure, cycling networks, and public transit over new road capacity", "Invest equally in road capacity and in multimodal options", or "Focus on road capacity and traffic flow", which is the dimension these rungs separate. The passage is adjacent and cannot support a chair.
